reading.body:
H.R. 9914 is a bipartisan bill with 23 cosponsors, and no lobbying filing from 2025 or later names it.

The cosponsor list is the substance here. A Republican sponsor, Robert Latta, is joined by 22 cosponsors split across both parties, including figures who recur on AI policy such as Jay Obernolte, Ted Lieu, Bill Foster, and Raja Krishnamoorthi. The bill's own text is tagged to jobs and workforce, frontier safety, and national security and exports. That combination of tags and that spread of cosponsors is what a bill looks like when it is being positioned as a consensus vehicle rather than a partisan one.

The absence of lobbying filings is the other half of the story. Zero filings for 2025 or later name this bill, which means the lobbying record so far shows no organized interest declaring it an issue. That is a statement about timing and disclosure as much as about influence. A bill can attract attention before it attracts filings, and a filing that names a bill records that the bill was an issue, not what position the filer took.

What this data does not cover is the bill's content, its committee path, or any vote. It records a sponsor, cosponsors, three issue tags, and a status date of 2026-07-23. Nothing here speaks to data centers, power, or compute, and it should not be read as if it did.
